push_headlines: Wall Street roared back Monday: the S&P 500 +4.73% to 7,237.17 and the Nasdaq +6.51% to 24,089.56, the best day since April 2025.
Europe rebounded as chipmakers led: the STOXX 600 +1.87% to 637.32, ending five straight daily declines.
Asia was split: the Kospi -3.30% to 4,708.54 while Taiwan's Taiex +2.20%; Tokyo was closed for a holiday.
on_notice: Monday's rebound followed Friday's slide into correction territory; watch whether Asia, led by Seoul and Tokyo's reopening, follows Wall Street higher tonight.
Oil slipped Monday, with Brent trading near $91.97 midmorning, as Iranian attacks on Strait of Hormuz shipping limited the losses.
Brazil's Ibovespa -0.95% to its lowest close since January 13 on fiscal-package worries; the real stays a pressure point.

asia.headline: Seoul sold off again while Taipei bounced; Tokyo was closed for a holiday.
asia.detail: The Kospi -3.30% to 4,708.54 after falling as much as 5.80% intraday on AI-bubble fears, while Taiwan's Taiex +2.20% after opening lower. In India the Nifty 50 -1.75% to 25,349.65.

china.headline: Hong Kong pared a near 2% early drop to finish about flat.
china.detail: The Hang Seng about -0.10% at the close after falling nearly 2% earlier in the session. No verified Shanghai Composite close was found, so none is quoted here.

europe.headline: European stocks snapped a five-day losing streak as chipmakers rallied.
europe.detail: The STOXX 600 +1.87% to 637.32 (a single report; treat as provisional) after a near 6% drop the previous week. Chipmakers ASML, ASM International and BE Semiconductor gained between 2.80% and 4.00% after Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO.

latam.headline: Brazil's Ibovespa fell to its lowest close since January 13.
latam.detail: The Ibovespa -0.95% to 164,796.05 as Petrobras weighed and caution over the fiscal package in the lower house grew. Hapvida -5.84% led the losers, while Magazine Luiza +9.63% led the gainers.

mideast.headline: Oil eased with the global selloff as Hormuz shipping attacks limited losses.
mideast.detail: Brent -0.65% to $91.97 and WTI near $82.92 by midmorning in London, per CNBC; no settlement price was found. Iranian attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz kept a floor under prices after Brent's third straight weekly loss.
